concepts.name: Drawing tools and mark types
concepts.summary: Name common drawing tools such as graphite grades, charcoal and erasers, and recall the kinds of marks each makes.

concepts.name: Grip and arm movement
concepts.summary: Explain how holding the pencil in different grips and moving from the shoulder, elbow or wrist changes line quality.

concepts.name: Line quality and pressure
concepts.summary: Understand how pressure and speed create light, dark, thick, thin, smooth or hesitant lines.

concepts.name: Basic shapes as building blocks
concepts.summary: Recognise circles, squares and triangles, and their 3D counterparts of spheres, cubes and cylinders, within everyday objects.

concepts.name: Contour and outline
concepts.summary: Understand that a contour line describes the edge of a shape and where forms turn or overlap.

concepts.name: Light and dark value
concepts.summary: Understand that value is how light or dark an area is, independent of colour, and that it makes forms read.

concepts.name: Seeing versus knowing
concepts.summary: Understand that drawing from observation means recording the actual shapes seen rather than remembered symbols.

misconceptions.text: Drawing is an innate talent that you either have or lack, not a learnable skill.
Erasing every imperfect line is the right way to draw accurately.
Shading means only pressing harder with the pencil.

concepts.name: Gesture and light construction lines
concepts.summary: Use quick, light lines to capture movement and overall placement before committing to final lines.

concepts.name: Measuring proportion by sighting
concepts.summary: Apply a pencil held at arm's length to compare relative lengths and angles of parts of a subject.

concepts.name: Negative space
concepts.summary: Draw the shapes between and around objects to check and correct the positive shapes.

concepts.name: One-point perspective
concepts.summary: Construct simple boxes and interiors with a horizon line and a single vanishing point, so receding lines converge.

concepts.name: Value scale and basic shading
concepts.summary: Produce a smooth range of values and use it to shade a sphere or cube with a light source.

concepts.name: Shading techniques
concepts.summary: Apply hatching, cross-hatching, stippling and smudging to build value for different effects.

concepts.name: Overlap and scale for depth
concepts.summary: Explain and use overlapping, relative size and placement on the page to suggest depth.

misconceptions.text: Measuring with a pencil is cheating and real artists draw purely by eye.
Parallel edges in a box always stay parallel in a drawing regardless of perspective.
Blending with a finger is the best way to make shading look smooth and realistic.

concepts.name: Two-point perspective construction
concepts.summary: Construct objects and buildings seen at an angle using two vanishing points on the horizon.

concepts.name: Ellipses and cylindrical forms
concepts.summary: Draw ellipses with correct minor axes to represent circles on receding planes and build cylindrical objects.

concepts.name: Light logic and cast shadows
concepts.summary: Analyse a light source to place highlight, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow consistently.

concepts.name: Compositional layout and framing
concepts.summary: Plan placement, cropping and focal points using thumbnails so the arrangement supports the subject.

concepts.name: Analysing observed relationships
concepts.summary: Analyse a subject for key angles, alignments and relative sizes to find and fix errors in a drawing.

concepts.name: Figure proportion and structure
concepts.summary: Use head-based proportions and simplified skeletal and volumetric forms to construct a standing figure.

concepts.name: Edge control and texture
concepts.summary: Vary hard, soft and lost edges and marks to describe surfaces such as metal, cloth or hair.

misconceptions.text: Circles viewed in perspective become ellipses with pointed ends.
Shadows can be placed wherever looks good without a consistent light source.
Placing the subject in the centre of the page is always the best composition.

concepts.name: Three-point and curvilinear perspective
concepts.summary: Analyse when vertical convergence or wide-angle distortion applies and construct scenes accordingly.

concepts.name: Atmospheric perspective and value hierarchy
concepts.summary: Analyse how contrast, detail and value range recede with distance and group values to unify a scene.

concepts.name: Complex form and anatomy
concepts.summary: Analyse underlying anatomy, planes and foreshortened forms to draw figures in varied poses convincingly.

concepts.name: Critique of drawing accuracy
concepts.summary: Evaluate a drawing against its reference, diagnosing proportional, tonal and structural errors and prioritising corrections.

concepts.name: Edge hierarchy for focus
concepts.summary: Judge and apply varied edge sharpness and contrast to direct attention to the focal point.

concepts.name: Efficient drawing process
concepts.summary: Evaluate and choose a workflow from large masses to details suited to the subject and time available.

concepts.name: Drawing from complex scenes
concepts.summary: Analyse busy subjects to select, simplify and restructure what to include while keeping believable space.

misconceptions.text: More detail everywhere makes a drawing more realistic.
Anatomy knowledge replaces the need to observe the actual pose.
Distant objects should have the same contrast as near ones as long as they are smaller.

concepts.name: Deliberate departure from realism
concepts.summary: Evaluate when bending proportion, perspective or value serves expression better than accuracy.

concepts.name: Personal visual language
concepts.summary: Create a consistent approach to line, value and abstraction that expresses an individual intent.

concepts.name: Drawing from imagination
concepts.summary: Create believable imagined subjects by combining stored knowledge of structure, light and perspective.

concepts.name: Narrative and mood in drawing
concepts.summary: Design compositions, lighting and gesture that convey a story or atmosphere.

concepts.name: Critical evaluation of drawings
concepts.summary: Evaluate drawings, including one's own and masters', against intent, technique and tradition with reasoned arguments.

concepts.name: Mixed media and surface choice
concepts.summary: Judge how materials and paper interact and combine media to realise an intended result.

concepts.name: Developing and teaching a practice
concepts.summary: Design a sustainable practice of studies, projects and feedback that drives continued growth and can guide others.

misconceptions.text: Developing a style means avoiding fundamentals and copying nothing.
Drawing from imagination can be done well without ever studying from life.
A technically accurate drawing is automatically a successful or expressive one.
